questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Why do cos θ and sin θ, read from the unit circle, always satisfy sin²θ + cos²θ = 1?
questions.prompt_markup: Why do cos θ and sin θ, read from the unit circle, always satisfy sin²θ + cos²θ = 1?

choices.text: Because sin θ + cos θ = 1 for every θ.
Because sin θ and cos θ are always equal.
Because the values were rounded so that they work.
The point (cos θ, sin θ) lies on the unit circle x² + y² = 1.

questions.correct_answer: The point (cos θ, sin θ) lies on the unit circle x² + y² = 1.
questions.grading_note: The coordinates satisfy the circle equation. The others are false (sin θ + cos θ = √2 at π/4; the values differ at π/6) or a non-reason.
